description:
Change of use from purely residential (Use Class C3) to mixed-use residential (Use Class C3) and professional medical services (Use Class E(e)).
I, Dr Robert Vardanyan, propose to use part of my residential property at 45 Kent Road, Chiswick, London, W4 5EY, for mixed-use purposes. 
The activities to be conducted at the premises will include medical consultations and services, procedures, therapy, all carried out in compliance with the standards set by the General Medical Council (GMC) and Care Quality Commission (CQC). These services will be provided GMC-registered medical practitioners and under the advice of the British Medical Association. All services will be carried out in accordance with professional medical licenses and CQC regulations.

Proposed Activities and Aims:
The work will serve as a valuable resource to the community by providing essential medical consultations and a range of medical services that support health and well-being, including mental health support and physical health services, tailored to meet the diverse needs of local residents. This commitment to health and support will not only benefit individual patients but also contribute positively to the overall health standards of the local area.

Consultation Frequency: 
The medical services will be offered on an appointment-only basis, ensuring that no patients are seen without prior scheduling. There will be no walk-ins or same-day appointments. Work will be on an infrequent basis due to being full-time NHS doctors. There will be no heavy foot traffic or large gatherings at the property.

Equipment and Machinery:
The proposed activities will require minimal equipment, such as examination beds and small medical instruments for minor procedures.
There will be no large-scale or heavy medical machinery installed at the premises. The activities carried out are non-invasive and do not require specialised equipment such as imaging machines.

Proposed Hours of Operation:
Medical services and consultations will be carried out between the hours of 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. As the appointments are pre-scheduled, there will be minimal disruption to the local area, with limited foot traffic and controlled entry to the building via an intercom system.

Foot Traffic: 
Given the nature of pre-booked consultations, the impact on the local neighbourhood will be minimal. Visitors will be limited in number, and there will be no large gatherings or unexpected guests.

Parking: 
Visitors will arrive individually and the current parking arrangements, such as visitor parkings, around the property are sufficient to accommodate the small number of visitors.

Noise: 
All activities conducted at the premises will be low-noise, with no machinery or loud equipment involved. There will be no significant noise pollution affecting neighbours or the surrounding area.
